cards.text: This is a song by David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster. Its first line sounds a lot like what Moses would say whenever the ark set out (Num 10:35). It starts simple: God arises.

cards.question: True or false: David says that when God arises, those who hate Him stand their ground.

cards.text: His enemies scatter and flee His presence. God drives them out like smoke blown away, and the wicked perish like wax melting before the fire.

cards.question: The wicked melt like wax before God. But David says the righteous do something very different before Him. What?

cards.text: Then David calls for a song to God, the One who rides on the clouds, whose name is the LORD. Friend, I get around by hopping on a little gold base, so yeah, we are NOT in the same league.

cards.question: True or false: David says the God who rides on the clouds is too high above it all to defend widows.

cards.text: God in His holy habitation is a father of the fatherless and a defender of widows. Friend, as a guy whose kids still call him Papa, that one hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: Right after the fatherless and the widows, David turns to the lonely. What does God do for them?

cards.text: God leads prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious live in a sun-scorched land. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so I'll take the being-led-out part, thank you VERY much.
Now David looks back and talks right to God. He remembers when God went out before His people and marched through the wasteland.

cards.question: When God marched through the wasteland, the earth shook before God, the One on ___.
The heavens poured down rain before God, and He sent abundant rain. What does David say that rain did for His weary inheritance?
God's flock settled in. From His bounty, who does David say God provided for?

cards.text: David's still singing about what God has done for His people. Now the Lord gives the command, and a great company of women proclaim it.

cards.question: A great company of women is spreading the Lord's news. What do they say kings and their armies do?
Kings and their armies are running. In the women's song, who divides the plunder?

cards.text: She stayed home and STILL got the goods, like missing the whole office cookie swap and walking out with a box anyway. Then the song pictures a dove with wings covered with silver and feathers with shimmering gold.
When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land, it was like the snow falling on Zalmon. Then David turns to Mount Bashan, a mountain of God, a mountain of many peaks.

cards.question: David asks the mountains of many peaks why they gaze in envy. What are they gazing at?

answers.text: The mountain God chose to dwell on

cards.question: True or false: David says the LORD will dwell on His chosen mountain only for a while.

cards.text: Then David pictures the chariots of God, and he gives us a number.

cards.question: True or false: David says the chariots of God number only in the hundreds.

cards.text: Tens of thousands. Thousands of THOUSANDS. Friend, I lose count of the chocolate chips in ONE batch.
The Lord is in His sanctuary as He was at Sinai. Then David tells God that He has ascended on high, led captives away and received gifts from men, even from the rebellious.

cards.question: God has ascended on high, led captives away and received gifts, even from the rebellious. What does David say it's for?

answers.text: So the LORD God may dwell there
So the nations will fear Israel
So the priests will have plenty

cards.text: Then David blesses the Lord, who daily bears our burden, the God of our salvation. DAILY, friend, not just the big days, but the snooze-button, where-are-my-keys days too.

cards.question: David calls God the God of our salvation and a God of deliverance. How far does he say the Lord GOD's rescue reaches?
True or false: David says God will make peace with those who persist in guilty ways.

cards.text: Instead, God will surely crush the heads of His enemies. And the Lord says He'll retrieve them from Bashan and bring them up from the depths of the sea, so that feet and dogs' tongues are dipped in the blood of the foes.
Now David pictures a parade. He says they have seen God's procession, as his God and King marches into the sanctuary.

cards.question: God's procession is marching into the sanctuary. Who does David say leads the way?

cards.text: Singers up front, musicians right behind, maidens playing tambourines among them. This is NOT a quiet entrance, friend, you can hear this crowd three streets over.

cards.question: True or false: As the procession arrives, David calls for God to be blessed in the great congregation.
In the procession, David points out ___, the youngest, ruling them.

cards.text: Benjamin's ruling them, with the princes of Judah, Zebulun and Naphtali in their company. Then David prays for God to summon His power, the strength He has exerted for David and his people.

cards.question: David says that because of God's temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring Him ___.

cards.text: Then David asks God to rebuke the beast in the reeds and the herd of bulls among the calves of the nations, until it submits, bringing bars of silver.

cards.question: David asks God to scatter certain nations. Which ones?

answers.text: The ones who delight in war
The ones who live far away
The ones who trade with Egypt

cards.question: David says envoys will arrive from Egypt. And Cush, a land south of Egypt, what does he say she'll do?

answers.text: Stretch out her hands to God
Send her armies to the north

cards.text: Then David calls the kingdoms of the earth to sing to God, who rides upon the highest heavens of old, whose mighty voice resounds. That's not a text to one friend, that's a reply-all to the WHOLE planet.

cards.question: True or false: David says God's majesty is over Israel and His strength is in the skies.
In the final verse, David says the God of Israel Himself gives His people something. What?

cards.text: David says God is awesome in His sanctuary, and he closes with "Blessed be God!" Thirty-five verses, friend, and I'm out of breath just hopping along behind it.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The question asks who divides the plunder inside the women's quoted line (v12). That means guessing the next words of the line, not reasoning from what came before. Nothing on the earlier cards points toward 'she who waits at home', so a right pick is luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The right answer 'She who waits at home' has a Bible-sounding phrasing ('She who…'). The wrong answers 'The kings' own servants' and 'The priests at the altar' sound plain, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only from his enemies', 'Only from hard times'). The right answer 'Even from death' is the only one built differently, so a baker can pick it by its shape.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card carries three things: God crushing His enemies' heads (v21), the Lord retrieving them from Bashan and the sea (v22), and feet and dogs' tongues dipped in the foes' blood (v23).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: In v22 the text doesn't say who 'them' is. The card puts 'He'll retrieve them' right after 'His enemies', which makes 'them' read as the enemies.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: A baker could argue the wrong answers are true elsewhere in the passage. 'Gold and silver': the dove's wings and feathers are covered with silver and shimmering gold, and she who waits at home divides the plunder (v12-13). 'Land and cattle': God's flock settled in His inheritance (v9-10).

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The card says 'Cush, a land south of Egypt'. That fact comes from outside the passage and has no reference in the card text. prep-walkthrough.md says outside facts like who a new person is come 'with their reference'. papa-dorin.md's 'New people' example ('Cyrus, king of Persia') has no reference. Stop 1 card 1 ('David, king of Israel') has the same question.
findings.question: When a card simply says who a new person is or where a new place is, does it need an inline Bible reference, or is the short description enough?
